checkpoint_review: The Router's checkpoint verdicts are generally reasonable. The Router correctly identified that many features (dorsal knuckles, full body shape, baleen, flippers, tail flukes) are not testable due to the spyhopping behavior showing only the head and upper body. The testable checkpoints (head shape, skin mottling, skin texture) were correctly marked as present. However, I note that the blowhole visibility claim is slightly generous - while the top of the head is visible, the actual blowholes are not clearly distinguishable in the image. The Router was appropriately conservative in marking untestable features as false rather than guessing.
artifact_review: The Router identified two minor artifacts: texture anomaly at the water-whale boundary (severity 1.5) and perspective distortion in the background horizon (severity 1.0). The topology_boundary_auditor returned a high mask confidence score (1.0068), which suggests the boundary is coherent, but this doesn't rule out subtle edge bleeding. The perceptual_quality_auditor found no graphics-level distortions. The geometric_depth_auditor's depth map shows reasonable depth distribution. However, I note that the water-whale boundary could have more subtle artifacts that the Router's severity rating of 1.5 might slightly underestimate. The background horizon distortion is minor but correctly identified. No major structural artifacts were found by experts or the Router.
alignment_reasoning: 4 out of 4 testable checkpoints passed. The fine_grained_classifier strongly confirms the image is a grey whale with high confidence (logit score 7.97, significantly higher than the second candidate at 2.62). The visible features (head shape, skin mottling, texture) match the taxonomy well. The Router was slightly lenient on blowhole visibility but this is a minor point. The untestable checkpoints were correctly excluded from scoring.
